steps.title: A trig equation is an intersection with a window
steps.body:
Nothing new in the method; three things are new in the details:
•  radians, unless the question says degrees
•  the window is the interval in the question: Xmin and Xmax are its ends
•  there are usually several crossings; the question wants all of them

\(2\sin2x=1\) on \(0\le x\le2\pi\): four crossings, \(x=0.262,\ 1.31,\ 3.40,\ 4.45\).

steps.title: Which window settings match the question?
steps.ok: ✓ Right. The x-window is the interval; the y-window just needs to show the curve.
bads: ✗ The standard window shows crossings outside \(0\le x\le2\pi\) too, and it is easy to report one of those by mistake. Match the window to the interval.
✗ \(360\) is degrees. The interval \(0\le x\le2\pi\) is radians: Xmax \(=2\pi\approx6.28\).

steps.title: How many solutions should there be?
steps.body:
Know the count before you press intersect, so a missing one is noticed:
•  \(\sin\) or \(\cos\) equal to a value strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\): two solutions per period
•  \(\sin(2x)\) has period \(\pi\), so \(0\le x\le2\pi\) holds two periods: four solutions
•  \(\sin(3x)\): period \(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\), three periods, six solutions

If a crossing sits exactly on an endpoint, check whether the interval includes it (\(\le\) or \(<\)).
steps.code:
period of \(\sin(bx)\) is \(\tfrac{2\pi}{b}\)
solutions on \(0\le x\le2\pi\): \(2\times b\) (for a value strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\))

steps.body:
List every solution in the interval, in radians, 3 s.f.:
•  the two graphs (or “by GDC”) and a sketch with the crossings marked

Exact forms (\(\tfrac{\pi}{12}\), \(\tfrac{5\pi}{12}\), …) are welcome but not required on Paper 2. Two habits that lose marks: one solution missing, and a value outside the interval included.

steps.title: tan, and intervals that start below zero
steps.body:
Two extra checks:
•  \(\tan x\) has period \(\pi\) and vertical asymptotes at \(x=\pm\tfrac{\pi}{2},\ \pm\tfrac{3\pi}{2},\ldots\); a horizontal line crosses it once per period, never at an asymptote
•  an interval like \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\) means Xmin \(=-\pi\): negative solutions are expected

\(\tan x=2\) on \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\): two periods, two solutions, \(x=-2.03\) and \(x=1.11\).

parts: How many solutions does \(\tan x=2\) have on \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\)?
Two: one per period of \(\tan\), and the interval holds two periods
✗ \(\tan\) crosses a horizontal line once per period (\(\pi\)); \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\) is two periods: two solutions.

Type the negative \(x\) to 3 significant figures.

steps.title: Models: the equation comes from the story
steps.body:
The height of water in a harbour is \(h(t)=3\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+5\) metres, \(t\) hours after midnight.
•  “when is the water \(6.5\) m deep?” means \(3\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+5=6.5\)
•  the interval is the time period asked about: the first \(12\) hours, \(0\le t\le12\)
•  the model is in radians (the \(\pi\) inside says so); answers are times, with units
